data.title: Pellagra — viva
data.summary: Nutritional & metabolic · 9 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Pellagra** (Nutritional & metabolic)_

**Q1. What is pellagra?**
- Systemic disease due to deficiency of niacin (vitamin B3 — nicotinic acid/nicotinamide) or its precursor tryptophan, with photosensitive dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia and death if untreated — the '4 Ds'
- 'Pelle agra' = rough skin (Italian)

**Q2. Discuss the causes of pellagra (PYQ).**
- Dietary: maize/jowar (sorghum)-based diets — niacin in maize is bound (niacytin) and maize has little tryptophan; sorghum has excess leucine which inhibits tryptophan–niacin conversion; poverty, famine, food faddism
- Alcoholism (commonest in India today), malabsorption (Crohn's, chronic diarrhoea, gastrectomy), anorexia nervosa, HIV, haemodialysis
- Drugs: isoniazid (competes with pyridoxine — needed for conversion), 6-mercaptopurine/azathioprine, 5-fluorouracil, pyrazinamide, ethionamide, phenytoin, phenobarbitone, chloramphenicol
- Carcinoid syndrome (tryptophan diverted to serotonin), Hartnup disease (defective neutral amino-acid transport — SLC6A19), deficiency of riboflavin/pyridoxine (cofactors)

**Q3. Describe the cutaneous features.**
- Symmetric, sharply demarcated photosensitive dermatitis on sun-exposed sites — dorsa of hands/forearms (gauntlet or glove), feet (boot), face (butterfly-like), neck (Casal's necklace — band around neck in C3/C4 dermatome), V of chest
- Acute: erythema, burning, blistering like sunburn; chronic: dry rough scaly hyperpigmented (dark-brown/'varnished') thickened skin with fissures; sharp upper border
- Perineal/genital involvement (friction), angular cheilitis, glossitis (red smooth swollen 'beefy' tongue), stomatitis, vulvitis/vaginitis

**Q4. Systemic features.**
- GI: diarrhoea, abdominal pain, nausea, anorexia (atrophy of mucosa)
- Neuropsychiatric: insomnia, irritability, depression, apathy, confusion, memory loss, psychosis, dementia, peripheral neuropathy; encephalopathy in alcoholics
- Weakness, weight loss; death if untreated

**Q5. How do you diagnose pellagra?**
- Clinical diagnosis with rapid response to niacin (therapeutic test)
- Supportive: low urinary N-methylnicotinamide and 2-pyridone (<1.5 mg/24 h), low serum tryptophan/niacin; check other deficiencies (B1, B2, B6, B12, folate, zinc), LFT (alcohol), 5-HIAA for carcinoid
- Histology non-specific: pallor of upper epidermis, hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, psoriasiform hyperplasia (similar to necrolytic migratory erythema, acrodermatitis enteropathica — 'deficiency dermatitis')

**Q6. Differential diagnosis.**
- Photosensitive drug eruption, polymorphic light eruption, chronic actinic dermatitis, airborne contact dermatitis, porphyria cutanea tarda, lupus (SCLE/DM), Hartnup disease, kwashiorkor, necrolytic migratory erythema, Bloom/Cockayne syndromes (children), carcinoid flushing

**Q7. Treatment.**
- Nicotinamide 100 mg every 6 h (or 300 mg/day) for 3–4 weeks then maintenance (nicotinamide preferred — no flushing); high-protein balanced diet; vitamin B-complex supplements (B1, B2, B6 deficits coexist), zinc
- Photoprotection, emollients for skin; stop alcohol/offending drug; treat carcinoid/malabsorption
- Response: mental symptoms improve within 24–48 h, skin in 1–2 weeks

**Q8. Discuss cutaneous manifestations of vitamin deficiencies (PYQ).**
- Vitamin A: xerosis, phrynoderma, night blindness, Bitot's spots, keratomalacia
- B2 (riboflavin): angular cheilitis, magenta tongue, seborrhoeic-like dermatitis, oral-ocular-genital syndrome
- B3 (niacin): pellagra
- B6: seborrhoeic dermatitis-like, cheilitis, glossitis, neuropathy
- B12/folate: hyperpigmentation (knuckles, palms), glossitis, angular cheilitis, canities
- Biotin: periorificial dermatitis, alopecia (raw egg-white avidin)
- Vitamin C (scurvy): perifollicular haemorrhage, corkscrew hairs, gingival bleeding, poor healing, woody oedema
- Vitamin K: purpura, ecchymoses
- Zinc: acrodermatitis enteropathica-like; essential fatty acids: xerosis, alopecia

**Q9. Discuss the role of zinc in dermatology (PYQ).**
- Cofactor for >300 enzymes (metalloproteinases, DNA/RNA polymerase, superoxide dismutase); needed for wound healing, immunity, keratinisation
- Deficiency: acrodermatitis enteropathica (inherited SLC39A4/ZIP4 defect; acquired — prematurity, low breast-milk zinc, TPN, malabsorption, alcoholism, nephrotic syndrome): periorificial and acral eroded psoriasiform dermatitis, alopecia, diarrhoea, paronychia, irritability, infections
- Therapeutic uses: acrodermatitis enteropathica (1–3 mg/kg/day elemental zinc), acne, warts, rosacea, leg ulcers, leishmaniasis, hidradenitis, erosive pustular dermatosis, as adjuvant in leprosy reactions

## Quick spotter facts
- Photosensitive dermatitis + Casal's necklace + diarrhoea + dementia — pellagra
- Maize diet, alcohol, isoniazid, carcinoid, Hartnup
- Nicotinamide — mind improves first

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Nutritional dermatoses). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
